name: Ausable Hall (Residence)
summary: A three-level buff-brick walk-up turning a broad blank end wall toward the drive, topped by a dark roof fascia with balconies along the long wings and lowest windows sitting close to grade.

evidence.note: Blank buff-brick drive-facing end in direct sun, with dark fascia flush to the wall. Brick sample #dec29b.
Tree covers the upper blank end. Outer corners and uninterrupted base visible.
Blank end with a dark cap and inset balconies on the adjoining wing. Three levels with a low garden floor.
Two offset flat-roofed ranges at a right angle, with a few small roof vents and no tall mechanical penthouse evident.
P50 7.71 m, P90 7.78 m, maximum 15.4 m above inventory ground. Continuous roof plateau near 7.7–7.8 m. The isolated 15.4 m maximum near trees does not track a second roof level.

notes: Only the south end and one adjoining elevation are photographed well. Long-wall bay counts, the courtyard door and balcony spacing are estimated from the university exterior photo and the related Beaver Hall block. Balcony slabs and solid side cheeks are pale concrete. The front rails are metal pickets. The south-end wall retains its two measured jogs. Three additional entrances are inferred from paths at the staggered ranges. Balconies have open pickets between solid pale end panels.
